The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d3ecf115570d0b89), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 36. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The nearby embeddings V0 can be partitioned into groups using one of the following three systems, together with the base-coordinate equations in (6.9) below: ⟨B, Y (a)P⟩ = r, r ∈ Mat2×2(Q), (1) ⟨B, Y (a)P⟩ = ⟨B′ , Y ′ (aR)P′ ⟩, R = a′ /a, (2) ⟨B, Y (a)P⟩ = ⟨I−1 0 B′ , Y (a)P̂⟩, P̂ = I−1 t P′ . (3) Here primes denote a simultaneous conjugate of the labeled data. Type (1) is used at infinity and at retained primes in S. At the other retained primes, type (2) is used if the coarse target pair lies outside the closed finite Hecke list of Proposition 3.4, and type (3) is used if it lies on that list. In types (2) and (3), the following additional data and properties hold at every assigned embedding: (i) |a′|v = |a|v, hence |R|v = 1, and h(R) ≤ Ch. (ii) There are two actual common reductions A and A ′ of the unprimed and primed center– target pairs, respectively. Relative Frobenius F : A −→ A ′ has polarized multiplier p and conjugates both labeled pairs to their primed counterparts. (iii) On each common reduction, smooth proper specialization at ℓ1 ̸= p preserves the two separately saturated plane lattices. Their reductions span the independent degenerate four-space prescribed by Proposition 4.2. (iv) In type (3), I0 = Ad(ϕ0) and It = Ad(ϕt) are conjugation isometries associated to polarized isogenies of the same fixed multiplier m∗. Their reductions satisfy ϕ0 = ϕt, and I0Y (a) = Y ′ (a′ )It. (6.7) Here p ∤ ℓ1m∗ and ℓ1 ∤ m∗. The maps induced by F and ϕ0 on ℓ1-adic Tate modules are integral isomorphisms, up to their unit similitude multipliers. The entries of r have bounded denominators and logarithmic heights at most C(1 + log h + log d). The pairs P̂ have fixed bounded denominators, polynomial Rosati norms, and all the coordinate bounds of Proposition 5.5.
